recorded.outcome:q-renderer-node: Page (Spot the Problem): "In `Shipment`, `this` is a `Shipment` to the compiler, whatever the object is at run time. A subclass that inherits `accept` instead of declaring its own has the same problem: it is handled as its parent." The output shows `s.accept(customs): skipped` for every class, and javap shows `Handler.visit:(LShipment;)` compiled into Shipment. Node/Heading/Table with a default render(Node) is the same setup, so the unsupported comment is decided. Summary: "One `accept` in the base class sends everything to the default."
recorded.prompt:q-subscribers: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-subscribers: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-subscribers: Page: `static int totalGrams(List<? extends Shipment> items) // reads Shipments`. "A `List<? extends Shipment>` could be a list of pallets, so the compiler won't add a letter to it." Reference table: `List<? extends T>` accepts "`List<T>`, `List<S>` for any subtype `S`", get is `T`, add takes "only `null`". This decides the key: the method accepts a List<EmailSubscriber>, reads elements as Subscriber and can't add. Minor point: "can't add one" holds for any Subscriber, but null can still be added. Implementing an interface counts as a subtype, which the page assumes without saying so.
recorded.prompt:q-three-rules: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-three-rules: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-three-rules: Page: "It keeps two classes (`TypeProfileWidth=2` on Java 21), so a third class leaves C2 with a virtual call, unless one class has at least 90 % of the calls". PrintInlining shows `== 3 class(es) ... virtual call`. Equal shares mean no class dominates, so the call stops being inlined, and the hot loop with a tiny body is where the page says this matters ("A few nanoseconds matter only when the method does as little as the call costs, in a loop that runs millions of times"). Caveat: the page bases the two-class limit on Java 21 (`TypeProfileWidth=2 on Java 21`), and the stem names no Java version.

recorded.outcome:q-renderer-node:d: Partly true: the result (unsupported comment) is right, but the reason is wrong. The page refutes it only indirectly. The double-dispatch output shows the same Handler with a default `visit(Shipment)` printing `CN22` for a Parcel when `visit(this)` is called with `this` declared as Parcel, so a default is not preferred over a specific overload. The page also gives the real reason, an overload chosen from the declared type. No sentence says outright that defaults don't take precedence.

"The interpreter and the first compiler tier record which classes reach each call site, and C2 reads that profile" shows interpretation is the profiling stage, not the result.
